description: The correlation rules of ADR-041 D3: how a failure travels along the relations. A rule names a relation type, optionally the class of its from and to ends (subclasses too), the source condition that triggers it (type and status) and the status of the impact it produces on the relation's dependant (relations.json), optionally only for a dependant whose attributes match `dependant` ({attribute: value}; true matches any value set), which then beats a rule without one. The controller refuses a rule it cannot place; health-manager rules list|check shows and validates them. Shipped: an operational critical crosses runs-on, depends-on, member-of and connects as critical impact, runs-on as a warning to a guest with haNode set (HA moves it), built-on from a disk to its pool, and stored-on from a pool to the guests and datastores on it; a warning crosses nothing.

rules.description: An HA-protected guest whose node fails is moving or has moved: degraded, not down.
A failed disk takes its pool down; in a mirror or raidz vdev (a redundancy group) it degrades it until every member has failed.
A failed pool takes down the guests and datastores whose data is on it; a degraded pool (a warning) reaches none of them.
A slow pool (ADR-046 D6) slows the guests and datastores whose data is on it: degraded, so "six guests are slow" derives to their pool.
A very slow pool degrades what is stored on it; it is not down, so the impact stays a warning.
A node under CPU or memory pressure slows the guests on it.
A node under heavy pressure degrades the guests on it; they still run.
